requirements.evidence: All contract classes are present with the exact signatures: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:14), UpdateQueue with nullable named params (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:13), SetQueueAccess (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:15), the QueuePermission enum with only `Call = 'call'`, the QueueAccess model with an array cast and membership()/queue() relations, a same-entity factory, and a migration with cascade FKs and unique (entity_membership_id, queue_id). Name trimming and the 1-255 length check, slug defaulting and slugifying, per-entity uniqueness, the self-slug exclusion on update (`where('id', '!=', $queue->id)`), and the no-log-on-empty-revoke rule are all implemented. CallNextTicket authorizes after the lock and active check (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:32). Ticket::call checks inactive, then authz, then the LogicException (app/Models/Ticket.php:95-107). There is no delete action. Gaps: the race mapping relies on fragile SQLSTATE/message sniffing (CreateQueue.php:59-69). Ticket::call reads the queue without lockForUpdate (Ticket.php:95).

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through app/Actions classes that each authorize inside with Gate::forUser()->authorize. Authorization lives in a single policy, app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php. The migration has a generated-style timestamp name (2026_10_29_072759_create_queue_access_table.php) and a reversible down(). Mass assignment is declared with #[Fillable([...])], matching Ticket.php. docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and the CHANGELOG 'Added' entry are all updated. PHPDoc on Ticket::call was updated to the new rule. No service or repository layers were added.

security.evidence: Every new action authorizes first, before any write (CreateQueue.php:16, UpdateQueue.php:15, SetQueueAccess.php:17). Both call paths now enforce the `call` ability (CallNextTicket.php:32, Ticket.php:105). The policy denies non-members, denies employees without a grant, and denies when a grant's permissions are not an array (QueuePolicy.php:45-71). A cross-entity membership/queue pair is rejected (SetQueueAccess.php:19). Permissions are whitelisted against the enum with strict in_array and an is_string check. $fillable is explicit. No exploitable weakness found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/QueueManagementTest.php covers: create with default and explicit slug, per-entity duplicates, blank and oversize names, denial for employee/outsider/other-entity owner with no writes, update including slug keep vs. conflict, update denial, grant and revoke audit context via a mocked channel, no log on an empty revoke, invalid and cross-entity grants, self-grant denial, every policy ability including the corrupted JSON case, the factory's same-entity invariant, unauthorized CallNextTicket in all three modes with tickets unchanged, an employee with a grant calling, and Ticket::call ordering (inactive first, authz before LogicException). Existing CallNextTicketTest cases were adapted by adding owner memberships, not weakened. Missing: the DB-unique race mapping, an upsert over an existing grant row, IssueTicket failing after deactivation through UpdateQueue, and a Ticket::call denial for an outsider on a waiting ticket.

simplicity.evidence: The code is generally direct. However, isUniqueViolation() is copy-pasted between CreateQueue.php:59 and UpdateQueue.php:82. It also hand-rolls detection that Laravel's UniqueConstraintViolationException already provides. The name/slug validation blocks are duplicated between the two actions. QueuePolicy::call re-implements the role check that isManager() already does (QueuePolicy.php:51-57 vs 75-81).

readability.evidence: Names are clear, methods are short, and the policy carries docblocks explaining the rules. Small blemishes in the tests: an unused `$owner` variable (tests/Feature/QueueManagementTest.php:187), and the test name 'allows an employee with a call grant to call, and checks inactive first on Ticket::call' (line 269) does not match what the test does. The test at line 250 issues two tickets on `$queue` that are never used by the per-mode loop.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: the actions, enum, model, factory, migration, policy, the call-path changes, docs, the CHANGELOG, and tests. The CallNextTicketTest edits are needed because callers now need a role. No UI and no delete action were added.

issues.explanation: Unique-violation detection treats any SQLSTATE 23000 (also FK/not-null violations) as a slug duplicate and misses PostgreSQL's 23505 / 'Unique violation' message; catching Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException would be correct and simpler.
The requirement that a DB unique-index race becomes a ValidationException has no test, and neither do upserting over an existing grant or IssueTicket failing after deactivation through UpdateQueue.
isUniqueViolation() and the name/slug validation are duplicated verbatim across the two actions.
The queue is read without lockForUpdate, so a concurrent deactivation is not serialized with the call the way CallNextTicket serializes it.
definition() eagerly persists an Entity even for make() or when the caller overrides both foreign keys.
There is an unused `$owner` variable, and the test name claims it checks the inactive queue first, but the test does not check that.

review.summary: The change adds CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess actions, the queue_access table/model/factory/enum, and a QueuePolicy enforced in both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call in the required order, with docs, a CHANGELOG entry, and a solid feature test suite. It meets the contract and project conventions with no security gaps; the remaining issues are fragile, duplicated unique-violation detection, a missing race test, and a few small test and readability blemishes, so it is approvable with nits.
